description: The two BIOS VRAM carve-out settings used on this machine, with the memory each one exposes. Values are read from server logs and a JSON recorded on the day; none is inferred.
machine: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 375 / Radeon 890M (gfx1150), 32 GB LPDDR5X

small.label: 0.5 GB carve-out
small.rocm_reported_vram_note: This is the GTT/UMA aperture the ROCm device exposes, not the 512 MiB dedicated carve-out.
small.full_offload_35b: works, via HIP unified memory oversubscribing into host RAM

large.label: 16 GB carve-out
large.gpu_addressable_note: Vulkan reports a 24,022 MiB total budget with this setting. That is the '24 GB usable' figure.
large.full_offload_35b: ROCm fails: the 16,679.34 MiB weight buffer exceeds the 16,384 MiB pool, and host RAM is too small to rescue it via unified memory. Vulkan succeeds.

consequence: The carve-out is a capacity trade-off, not a quality setting. Raising it from 0.5 GB to 16 GB moves about 15.5 GiB out of host RAM and into the GPU pool. Vulkan benefits; ROCm's full-offload path for this 16.79 GiB model does not, because one contiguous 16,679 MiB allocation cannot fit in a 16,384 MiB pool and the remaining host RAM is too small to back it.
status: Operator-confirmed on 2026-11-08 that both settings were used. The per-run setting of the two archived llama-bench files (2026-09-30 ROCm, 2026-10-01 Vulkan) is not recorded in those files.
